Birmingham is a thriving area with strong demand for reliable new boiler supply and installation services. Local properties range from period Victorian and Edwardian homes through to modern new-build developments, each presenting different plumbing requirements and challenges.

Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of Birmingham and the surrounding West Midlands region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional boiler installation services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across West Midlands, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any new boiler supply and installation requirement.

We cover all postcodes across Birmingham with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: Do I need a combi boiler or a system boiler?
faqs.a: Combi boilers suit most homes up to 3 bedrooms with 1-2 bathrooms — no hot water tank needed. System boilers suit larger homes with higher hot water demand. Your installer should calculate your requirements before recommending.

faqs.q: What is the best boiler brand?
faqs.a: Worcester Bosch, Viessmann, and Vaillant consistently top reliability surveys. All three offer extended warranties of 8-12 years when installed by accredited engineers. Brand matters less than correct sizing and installation quality.

faqs.q: Do I need to notify anyone when a new boiler is installed?
faqs.a: Yes — your Gas Safe registered installer must notify Building Control within 30 days of installation under the Competent Person Scheme. You will receive a Building Regulations completion certificate.

faqs.q: How much can a new boiler save on energy bills?
faqs.a: Replacing a G-rated boiler (pre-2005) with an A-rated condensing boiler can save £300-£500 per year on gas bills. The actual saving depends on your home size, insulation, and usage patterns.

localParagraph: Birmingham's diverse housing stock — from the Victorian terraces of Balsall Heath and Stirchley to the post-war semis of Erdington and the modern new-builds springing up across Digbeth — means that boiler installation across the city rarely follows a single template. Engineers working throughout Birmingham must assess each property individually, accounting for older pipework, varying system pressures, and the region's mixed water hardness, which sits somewhere between soft and hard depending on the specific postcode. This moderate mineral content means scale build-up is a genuine consideration, and reputable installers will often recommend a magnetic filter or inhibitor treatment alongside any new boiler to protect the heat exchanger and extend the unit's working life. England's building regulations apply consistently across the West Midlands, so all installations must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer and comply with current Part L efficiency standards. Whether you're replacing an aging back boiler in a Handsworth terrace or fitting a combi unit in a city centre apartment, choosing an experienced local installer ensures the work is completed safely and to the correct specification.
whatItInvolves: A new boiler installation involves removing your existing unit, upgrading the flue and pipework where required, fitting and commissioning the new boiler, and registering it with Building Control via the Competent Person Scheme. All new boiler installations must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer — it is illegal for anyone else to do this work.
process: Day 1: drain down the system, remove the old boiler, cap off existing connections. Upgrade the flue if required — most modern boilers use a concentric flue that vents through an external wall. Fit the new unit, connect flow and return pipes, gas supply, and condensate drain. Commission the boiler following manufacturer guidelines, balance the radiators, and register the installation. You'll receive a Building Regulations completion certificate within 28 days.
whatToExpect: A standard like-for-like boiler swap takes 1-2 days. A full system change — moving the boiler or converting from back boiler to combi — takes 2-4 days. Your new boiler should come with a manufacturer warranty of 5-12 years depending on brand. Always register the warranty within 30 days of installation.
